Basin Weekly

The Quiet Fight Over Groundwater

Farmers in the invented Tesh Basin have pumped groundwater faster than rain replaces it for thirty years, and the wells that once reached water at forty feet now go down more than two hundred. A new state rule will cap pumping for the first time, and the fight over who gives up water first has already reached the courts.

The rule asks each district to submit a plan that brings pumping back into balance by 2040. Districts that fail to agree on a plan will have one written for them by the state water board, which has said it would cut every user by the same share.
